title: Teaching Gemini to Speak YouTube: Adapting LLMs for Video Recommendations to 2B+DAU - Devansh Tandon
talk_summary: Google adapted a Gemini checkpoint into a 'Large Recommender Model' for YouTube by inventing a semantic-ID tokenization of videos, continued pre-training to link text and video tokens, then prompting with user context for generative retrieval. The main practical lessons are about serving-cost reduction and precomputing expensive LLM inference into offline lookup tables.

takeaways.technique: Precompute expensive LLM inference into an offline lookup table
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of running the expensive personalized model per request, they strip personalization, run the same prompt offline over the head of the corpus, and serve recommendations via a simple lookup.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we tried to turn this into an offline problem... build just an offline recommendations table... we can just do a simple lookup to serve some recommendations
takeaways.numbers: 95%+ serving cost savings cited for the online path

takeaways.technique: Aggressively shrink the serving model to hit cost/latency
takeaways.what_they_do: They found the big model too expensive to serve at scale and moved to smaller checkpoints (flash and smaller) to meet latency and scale requirements.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's no way that you can serve that to billions of daily active users... we had to focus on the smaller, more efficient models

takeaways.technique: Train/eval on the tasks that matter most, not the whole space
takeaways.what_they_do: They built task- and surface-specific aligned models (retrieval vs ranking) rather than one general model, and measured gains on their hardest tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can align it for different recommendation related tasks like retrieval and ranking... make a small custom version of this model for all of the major recommendation surfaces

takeaways.technique: Compress domain objects into compact semantic tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: They quantize rich multi-feature video representations into a handful of semantically meaningful tokens so the model can reason over many items within limited context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even with a million tokens of context, when you want to reason over many videos, you have to compress that video representation in some way

takeaways.technique: Separate capability experts to avoid catastrophic forgetting
takeaways.what_they_do: When over-training on the domain language degraded English ability, they explored mixture-of-experts so some experts retain text capability while others specialize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as you overtrain on more and more of those examples actually the model forgets to speak English
